# Remove-ZbxTriggerPrototype

## SYNOPSIS

Removes trigger prototypes.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxTriggerPrototype [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTriggerPrototype>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A trigger prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one trigger per entity it finds. The Remove-ZbxTriggerPrototype cmdlet deletes the trigger prototypes given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with triggerprototype.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete a trigger prototype

```powershell
Remove-ZbxTriggerPrototype -InputObject 'Free space is low on {#FSNAME}' -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the trigger prototype Free space is low on {#FSNAME}. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the trigger prototypes a search finds

```powershell
Get-ZbxTriggerPrototype -Name 'Free*' | Remove-ZbxTriggerPrototype -WhatIf
```

Lists the trigger prototypes whose names start with Free that the command would delete, and deletes nothing.
